cluster.definition: Each rendered stimulus is a distinct body; resample the 61 stimuli.

cohort.construction: One DAZ Genesis base model manipulated on a single thinness/fatness continuum; heads removed; white underwear and undershirt.

dataset: Moussally et al. body-only computer-generated pictures of women

identity.definition: Each rendered stimulus appears once, so this set cannot measure multi-photo identity stability.

label.definition: mean body valence from attractiveness, beauty, and harmony judgments
label.independence: The shipped CNN was trained on Connor full-body photographs, not these 61 Moussally synthetic body-only stimuli; no result from this set selected the shipped model.
label.limitation: The valence aggregate includes attractiveness, beauty, and harmony and is not an attractiveness-only judgment.
label.raters: N=77-82 young women per stimulus because of missing data

license.repository_policy: no source images committed; only hashes, factual labels, and aggregates
license.restriction: do not distribute stimuli without explicit author consent

limitations: Synthetic female-presenting bodies from one generated shape continuum do not represent natural photographic diversity.
The dataset has no male bodies and no legitimate human demographic subgroup labels.
Each body appears once, so it cannot estimate multi-photo identity stability.
The body-valence aggregate is body-specific but not attractiveness-only.
